Subject: Question on uptime tiers + surge coverage for Dedicated pool

Hi Jasmine,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the Dedicated capacity performance looked great. Before we push this through procurement I need to clarify a couple of items around SLA and premium support packaging so I can include them in our internal MLP: 

- Uptime ladder: can you confirm the concrete uptime bands you offer (e.g., 99.9 / 99.95 / 99.99) and the corresponding credit schedules? Do credits roll forward or are they per-month buckets?
- Response times: what are the guaranteed L1/L2 response windows for each tier, and how do on-call rotas factor for weekends/holidays?
- Surge / on-call credits: we anticipate occasional burst events during peak product launches — can you outline how surge coverage is billed and what discounts are available for committed volume?

Also, procurement asked for a single-page summary and a sample statement we can send to legal documenting the escalation path. Is that something you can provide this week?

Appreciate a short call if that’s easier.

Best,
Elena
Procurement Manager
Brightlane Systems

Elena — thanks for the clear list. I’ve drafted a concise summary and an initial pricing spreadsheet to show the blended economics for Dedicated capacity + premium support. I attached:
- sla_pricing_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet): uptime bands, credit slab, per-seat & per-gpu pricing, and surge-credit examples
- proposal_brightlane_v2.pdf (one-page summary and escalation path language)

Quick answers inline:
- Uptime bands: we typically quote 99.9 / 99.95 / 99.99. Credits are calculated per-calendar-month against committed throughput; we can offer quarterly true-ups for enterprise contracts.
- Response times: Standard (included) = 4-hour business-hours response (L2 triage) for P1, Premium = 1-hour 24x7 for P1 with named on-call escalation. You can mix & match per-route.
- Surge/on-call credits: bursts are billed on consumed tokens/compute; for firms with committed GPU pools we provide a surge-credit pool (prepaid credits that consume at a reduced rate) and a volume-based discount at renewal.

I’ve suggested a conservative discount ladder in the sheet; happy to run the numbers for your expected monthly committed throughput if you share a baseline. Would you be available for a 30-min call Tuesday to finalize the language for legal?

Best,
Jasmine Liu
Account Executive — Enterprise
Redwood Inference

Jasmine — skimming your sheet. A few internal notes (high-level):

- Margin: the surge-credit pool as prepaid at a 30% discount vs on-demand looks attractive to them but it eats into margin if we bend too deep below list. Suggest cap discount at 20% for first-year commit with step-down incentives based on renewal volume.
- Uptime bands: 99.99 requires an HA topology and cross-zone failover; factor in regional standby GPUs for the Dedicated pool (we should call out the incremental cost per standby node).
- Response windows: offering 1-hour 24x7 is heavy; recommend Premium (1-hour) as an add-on seat-based SKU rather than wholesale on whole account for first year.

Suggested negotiation script for discord with procurement:
- Offer 99.95 w/ quarterly true-up as baseline; include optional 99.99 add-on with standby node pricing.
- Provide surge-credit pool at 20% off if they commit to >=6 months of prepaid credits.
- If they push for deeper discounts, protect margin with a minimum committed $/month or a blended effective-rate floor.

If you want, I can draft one alternate quote (conservative) and one stretch quote (commercial) for the call.
